summary_oneline: Auto-detect an available coding-agent CLI (Claude Code, then Codex) and default wikitoolkit/bookstore's unset LLM env vars to it, with a visible warning and an opt-out.

localization.role: single shared LLM-resolution seam for bookstore CLI + MCP server; currently returns (None, None, None) when PARROT_BOOKSTORE_LLM is unset
degraded-mode stand-in; ask_structured() raises the exact 'No LLM configured for the bookstore' error the requester observed
resolves WIKI_EXTRACT_LLM, skips extraction (not an error) when unset
generic 'flag or env, else ClickException' resolver used by ingest-style commands
builds the lightweight+heavy PageIndexLLMAdapter pair via LLMFactory.create; documents a same-provider constraint between light/heavy
already-registered AbstractClient wrapping claude-agent-sdk / the claude CLI; strictly lazy SDK import
registers ClaudeAgentClient under claude-agent and claude-code provider keys
symmetric already-registered client wrapping the codex CLI; codex_bin='codex', default_model='gpt-5.1-codex', lazy _import_sdk()
registers OpenAICodexClient under codex-agent / openai-codex / codex-code provider keys
existing enum value 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' — the cheap/deterministic model id the requester asked for
existing precedent naming the three canonical coding-agent CLI identifiers (codex/claude/gemini), but for wiki-hook installation, not LLM defaulting — not directly reusable

constraints.statement: Neither bookstore nor wikitoolkit hardcodes a default LLM provider today; unset env vars are a deliberately supported degraded mode (BM25/deterministic carding only), not a bug.
constraints.implication: the proposal is a genuine philosophy change (documented explicitly, per the requester's own framing) and must say so plainly rather than being framed as 'fixing a wrong default'

constraints.statement: PageIndexToolkit pairs the heavy adapter's client with the lightweight model id internally, so light/heavy must resolve to the same provider.
constraints.implication: an auto-detected default must pick one provider and apply it to both WIKI_MODEL and WIKI_LIGHTWEIGHT_MODEL (and PARROT_BOOKSTORE_LLM / PARROT_BOOKSTORE_LLM_LIGHT) together, never mix

constraints.statement: Both ClaudeAgentClient and OpenAICodexClient already exist, are registered in LLMFactory, and guard their real SDK import behind a lazy, exception-safe helper.
constraints.implication: no new client code is needed; detection can safely mirror the same 'try: import <sdk>' idiom plus a `shutil.which(<cli_bin>)` check, with zero subprocess/network calls during detection itself

constraints.statement: A cheap, deterministic Claude model id (ClaudeModel.HAIKU_4_5 = 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001') already exists; no equivalent cheap Codex model id was found in this research pass (only default_model='gpt-5.1-codex').
constraints.implication: the Claude Code default model choice is fully grounded; the Codex default model choice is not — flagged as an unknown rather than guessed

constraints.statement: wiki/coding_agents.py already treats 'codex', 'claude', and 'gemini' as the three canonical coding-agent CLI identifiers for a different purpose (installing wiki-nudge hooks).
constraints.implication: the new detection helper should reuse the same three identifiers/naming for consistency, even though it can't reuse the code

new: A shared, provider-agnostic detection helper (proposed location: `packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/clients/detection.py`) exposing something like `detect_coding_agent_llm() -> Optional[str]` that returns an `LLMFactory` spec string (e.g. `claude-code:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) or `None`, using only `shutil.which(cli_bin)` + a lazy SDK-importable check — never a real request.

modified.change: resolve_adapter() falls back to the detection helper when PARROT_BOOKSTORE_LLM is unset, before returning degraded (None, None, None); logs a visible warning naming the auto-selected spec and the override env var
the three resolution points (_extract_into_graph, _resolve_model_id, _build_triage_adapters call sites) fall back to the same detection helper instead of erroring/skipping when their env var is unset

untouched: ClaudeAgentClient and OpenAICodexClient themselves — no client-level code changes, this is purely a defaulting/detection layer above LLMFactory.create()
The existing explicit-config path (PARROT_BOOKSTORE_LLM / WIKI_MODEL / WIKI_LIGHTWEIGHT_MODEL / WIKI_EXTRACT_LLM set by the user) — always takes precedence over auto-detection, unchanged
Gemini/Google support — remains fully available as an explicit choice, just never auto-selected
patterns_to_follow: Lazy heavy imports under stdout→stderr redirect, matching _llm.py's existing 'safe to import from the MCP server' constraint (F001/F003)
The 'try: import <sdk>; except ImportError' idiom already used inside ClaudeAgentClient/OpenAICodexClient (F008)
Never fail startup on detection/resolution failure — always degrade gracefully with a warning, matching the existing except Exception: return None, None, None pattern (F003)
integration_risks: Silent behavior change on any machine that happens to have `claude` or `codex` on PATH but where the user did NOT intend wikitoolkit to spend their coding-agent session/budget on background summarization — mitigated by the visible-warning + opt-out requirement from the source request, but the exact opt-out mechanism is still an open question (see unknowns)
Precedence when both `claude` and `codex` CLIs are detected on the same machine is unresolved — needs a deterministic, documented rule (see unknowns)

unknowns.question: When both a `claude` and a `codex` CLI are detected on the same machine, which provider should win by default?
plausible_answers: Claude Code always wins (matches the source request's framing, and this codebase is 'AI-Parrot' built primarily around Claude workflows)
First one found wins, in a fixed check order (e.g. claude, then codex) — same practical effect as (a) unless codex-only
Configurable via an env var (e.g. PARROT_AUTO_LLM_PREFERENCE=claude-code,codex) with the above as the built-in default order
unknowns.user_answer: Claude Code always wins by default.

unknowns.question: What should the opt-out mechanism be called, and should it disable auto-detection everywhere at once or per-subsystem (bookstore vs wikitoolkit)?
plausible_answers: One global env var, e.g. PARROT_NO_AUTO_LLM=1, disabling auto-detection for both subsystems
Two scoped env vars mirroring the existing PARROT_BOOKSTORE_LLM / WIKI_* naming
No separate opt-out var at all — setting any explicit *_LLM env var already opts out per-subsystem, and that's enough
unknowns.user_answer: One global env var, PARROT_NO_AUTO_LLM=1, disabling auto-detection for both bookstore and wikitoolkit at once.

unknowns.question: Since no cheap/deterministic Codex model id was found in this pass (only default_model='gpt-5.1-codex'), what model id should the Codex fallback use, or should Codex auto-defaulting be deferred to a follow-up until that's confirmed?
plausible_answers: Use OpenAICodexClient.default_model ('gpt-5.1-codex') as-is — Codex CLI billing/model selection may not expose a cheaper tier the same way Claude does
Defer Codex auto-defaulting entirely to a fast-follow proposal; ship Claude Code detection only in this feature
The requester already knows the right Codex model id from personal usage and can supply it directly
unknowns.user_answer: Use OpenAICodexClient.default_model ('gpt-5.1-codex') as-is; ship Codex detection in this same feature (not deferred).

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence across both subsystems and both required clients already exist and are registered — the remaining unknowns are small, user-answerable policy choices (precedence, opt-out naming, Codex model id) that a spec's Open Questions section can carry into implementation, not architectural forks that would need a brainstorm.
